subject: Rate limits / burst guardrails and overage paths — follow-up from discovery
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Mills <lauren.mills@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 18 Jul 2026 16:02:00 -0700
Subject: Follow-up & numbers — burst behavior, budget target ($/1M tokens)

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the call earlier — really helpful to hear how Acme Health plans to use LLMs across clinical summaries and triage routing. Quick recap and a few clarifying items so we can lock down a pricing path and rate-limit guardrails.

Recap (as I heard it):
- Primary workload: near-real-time clinical summarization for in-app notes, average prompt+response ~1.2k tokens, peak concurrent users ~80, steady-state concurrency ~15.
- Daily volume: expected ramp from ~10M tokens/day (pilot) to ~200M tokens/day in 6–9 months.
- Hard budget guidance: $800–1,200 per 1M tokens target as a blended unit cost (including any caching/batching savings) — you said $/1M tokens is a helpful lens for procurement.
- Key ask: predictable latency <250ms p95 for short requests; ability to burst without immediate hard throttling during spikes (e.g., overnight ingestion jobs).

Clarifying questions:
1) The 200M tokens/day estimate — is that measured in input-only tokens or input+output combined? (We assumed input+output when modeling cost above.)
2) How often do you expect ingestion-style bursts versus interactive user bursts? Rough % of traffic that can be delayed / queued.
3) Any procurement constraints on overage billing (pre-approval needed for monthly overages, or allow a one-time auto-bill up to X%)?

Proposed next steps (internal + procurement):
- We’ll produce a short rate-limit & overage options doc: 1) soft-burst + auto-queue, 2) reserved commit with burst credits, 3) hard-limit with pre-approved overage.
- Ben (SE) will share expected token unit-economics by model family and recommended batching/quantization levers based on your sequence lengths.
- If the $800–1,200 /1M tokens is a firm target, we’ll show a 3-month rollout plan to hit that blended rate with a mix of caching and Dedicated burst credits.

Attaching a preliminary pricing estimate and a short rate-limit proposal (draft). We left placeholder numbers for the final volume mix.

Are you available next Tuesday (7/21) for a 30-min follow-up with procurement? If not, suggest a couple of times and we’ll accommodate.

Thanks —
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0172

Attachments: rdw_pricing_estimate_q3_v2.xlsx, rate_limit_proposal.pdf
From: Lauren Mills <lauren.mills@acmehealth.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 19 Jul 2026 09:24:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & numbers — burst behavior, budget target ($/1M tokens)

Hi Vanessa — thanks for the clear recap. Correcting a couple of items and answering your questions inline.

1) Volume metric: our forecasts were in input+output combined (so please keep that assumption).
2) Bursts: roughly 65% interactive (user-driven) and 35% ingestion (batch jobs). Ingestion spikes happen nightly—can be 3–4x baseline for short 20–40 minute windows. Interactive spikes are unpredictable but shorter.
3) Procurement: we need an overage approval process. Typically procurement will approve a one-off overage up to 20% of committed spend with auto-billing; anything beyond that needs explicit sign-off.

Also — the $800–1,200/1M is a soft target. The finance team would prefer the lower half for sustained volumes; for pilot months they can tolerate the high end.

I can do Tue 7/21 at 11am PT for a 30-min call with procurement and engineering. Please include your SE and any docs that explain burst-credit mechanics.

Best,
Lauren Mills
Director, AI Platforms | Acme Health
lauren.mills@acmehealth.com
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Mills <lauren.mills@acmehealth.com>
Cc: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 20 Jul 2026 08:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Follow-up & numbers — burst behavior, budget target ($/1M tokens)

Hi Lauren — thanks for the clarity. Quick technical notes and a concrete option set so procurement can evaluate.

Short answers first: yes, we treat the volumes as input+output by default. For your mixed spike profile, we recommend:

Option A — Reserved Commit + Burst Credits (Recommended for your goal):
- Commit: monthly reserved capacity sized to cover p90 steady-state (this reduces per-1M token unit cost).
- Burst credits: each month you get X credits equal to 50% of committed capacity for short bursts; credits regenerate monthly.
- Soft-burst behavior: requests beyond commit use burst credits automatically (no throttling until credits exhausted), with best-effort latency.
- Overage: once credits are exhausted, overflow goes to on-demand pricing at a defined overage rate. Procurement-friendly: we can set an auto-bill cap (e.g., 20% over commit) that requires approval beyond that.

Option B — Auto-queue + Adaptive Batching (Lower cost, higher tail latency):
- Spikes are throttled into a short FIFO queue (max queue depth configurable) with adaptive batching to keep unit-cost low.
- Good for ingestion-heavy bursts where slight delay (seconds to a minute) is acceptable.
- Overage: minimal because excess work is deferred, not billed immediately as on-demand.

Option C — Hard limit with pre-approved overage windows (tighter control):
- Hard token rate limit enforced; you get immediate rejection if limit hit unless a pre-approved overage window is opened by procurement.
- Best for strict cost-containment and procurement workflows.

Unit economics: preliminary blended rates (input+output, after simple prefix caching & batching)
- Dedicated commit model (p90 steady): ~$650–900 /1M tokens depending on model family and quantization.
- On-demand: ~$1,100–1,600 /1M tokens depending on model.
- With aggressive batching and KV caching we can show a path to the lower bound of your target within 8–10 weeks after rollout.

Action items for Tue 7/21 11am PT:
- Vanessa: bring the pricing estimate and the draft rate_limit_proposal.pdf (you have it attached already)
- Lauren: procurement will confirm auto-bill cap policy and who can approve >20% overage
- Ben: I’ll prepare a 2-slide SE summary showing latency expectations for soft-burst vs queued options and a worked example of cost at 200M tokens/day.

If useful, I can also include a short guarantee language for SLA/latency on reserved capacity and an emergency escalation path for unplanned ingestion events.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com
